title: What does XChainCommit do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XChainCommit and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, XChainCommit starts a cross-chain transfer by committing value to a configured bridge. [1]

The destination side relies on witness attestations and claim processing rather than assuming every source submission is final. Check the bridge, asset, amount and claim identifier. A validated source commitment is useful evidence of the first stage, but the recipient's final delivery needs its own destination-chain confirmation. [1]

The XChainCommit reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using XChainCommit, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
